evals.name: verify-existing-paper
evals.prompt: A colleague is going to review out/factory_farming/paper_attribution_v1 next week and I want to know it'll hold up before they see it. Can you actually check it rather than skim the tex — does it have the tables and figures it should, and is every number in it real?
evals.expected_output: A verdict backed by evidence: pages rendered and inspected, numerals audited mechanically against declared artifacts, specific defects named or an explicit all-clear.

evals.name: fix-unresolvable-overlay
evals.prompt: I drafted configs/run/paper_broken_v1.yaml for a short paper on the form result but I can't get it to build. Can you get it working? Don't burn API budget guessing — I've been billed for a couple of failed runs already.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses defects WITHOUT running the full writeup first (primary_reading not in source_runs; trajectory_run pointing at a run with no trajectory.jsonl; af_summary contrast citing a run absent from source_runs), fixes them, and demonstrates evidence resolves.

evals.name: scope-revision-after-falsification
evals.prompt: H30 just got falsified — a real embedding retriever (E5) ranks our installed ladder at rho +0.94, way above the word-count baseline, and it doesn't trip the null-cell trap. Does paper_attribution_v1 need to change? Do whatever's actually right here.
evals.expected_output: Determines the paper is scoped to gradient methods and therefore NOT contradicted, rather than panic-editing; identifies that the scope sentence is now backed by a counterexample; distinguishes ranking from removal; may update PAPER_AUDIT/PROPOSAL rather than the paper.
